svg.text: Who calls whom (part 1), and what one acquisition does, step by step (part 2). Arrows point from the caller to what it uses.
1. Components — layers and who calls whom
API · JobFetchProbe.Api (controllers use Services only; creates and upgrades the database at start-up)
JournalController GET api/Journal/... (runs, entries after N)
Services · JobFetchProbe.Services (the rules; knows only Models and its own interfaces)
one at a time · background task
Stop, or API stops → run stops cleanly
one DI scope per step · records journal
start recorders · read runs and entries
Abandoned: 2 min without sign of life
JobDetailsFetcher: one job at a time
RunRecorderCore: queue, sign of life 30 s
writes never stop or slow a step
Services/Abstractions — the interfaces Services needs: IInputFolder · ISavedPageReader · IPageFetcher | IBatchRepository · IJobRepository · IJobCatalog · IJournalRepository
Data · SQLite with EF Core (implements; entities never leave)
saved search pages you put here
Listings · ListingSources · ListingJobs · Jobs · JobDetails (see database.svg)
Red markers: places that are not idempotent yet — see docs/backlog.md, section 5.
this process, or the journal says a run
is Running with a sign of life < 2 min
the run goes on in the background
journal recorder for each step (on the side)
cancel: Stop · API stopping → after current page or job
Step 1 · FetchJobListing — saved pages → listing (no network)
bad page / bot check → kept in input/
only after the listing is stored
Step 2 · FetchJobDetails — every job without a description, one at a time
jobs not Read and not Gone
Opened → after the cooldown the same job is tried once more (trial request). Closed again → normal pace.
Opened StopAfterOpenings (3) times → the run stops; the next run continues with what is left.
On the side: the journal (any process can read it while the run goes on)
every page, job and circuit change → recorder → background queue
→ journal tables in jobs.db · sign of life every 30 s · 2 min without one → Abandoned
GET api/Journal/runs, then GET api/Journal/<step>/runs/{id}?after={last entry id}
every few seconds until the state is no longer Running: Completed · Stopped · Failed · Abandoned
